severityAudit.title: Zero Exchange Rate Bypass Allows Unconfigured Token Exploitation

analysis.assetRisk: Value extraction only if admin fails to configure token - not direct theft by attacker alone
analysis.attackPath: INVALID - Requires admin misconfiguration (adds strategy without calling setTokenConfig). This is a hypothetical precondition.
analysis.conditions: Admin must add 6-decimal token strategy without configuring decimals. Default fallback assumes 18 decimals, causing incorrect scaling.
analysis.impact: If triggered, significant value extraction possible. However, trigger requires admin operational error.

severityAudit.disagreementReason: Finding requires external conditions (admin misconfiguration) that disqualify it from High severity per C4 criteria. 'Admin forgets to call setTokenConfig()' is a hypothetical scenario. Per C4: High requires attack path 'without hypotheticals'.
severityAudit.recommendation: Downgrade to Medium. Reframe as 'Missing token configuration validation in addYieldStrategy()'. Consider adding config requirement check or revert in claim() if token not configured.
severityAudit.notes: The code actually has a reasonable default (assumes 18 decimals, 1:1 rate) - the bug only affects non-18-decimal tokens. This is a decimal scaling issue, not zero exchange rate.

severityAudit.title: collectReward Call Does Not Verify Token Transfer

analysis.assetRisk: Tokens potentially stuck in accumulator - but only if Phlimbo has implementation bug
analysis.attackPath: INVALID - Root cause is hypothetical bug in external Phlimbo contract, not in audited code
analysis.conditions: Requires Phlimbo.collectReward() to fail to properly transferFrom tokens. This is speculation about external contract behavior.
analysis.impact: If Phlimbo is buggy, tokens stuck. But this is Phlimbo bug, not accumulator bug.

c4CriteriaCheck.externalRequirements: N/A - root cause is out of scope

severityAudit.disagreementReason: The finding's root cause is the assumption that Phlimbo may not properly implement collectReward(). Per C4: 'Issues in parent/forked contracts where root cause is OOS' are out of scope. The accumulator correctly transfers tokens to itself and calls Phlimbo - if Phlimbo fails, that is Phlimbo's bug.

scopeAnalysis.auditeCodeBehavior: Correct - transfers tokens, calls external interface as documented
scopeAnalysis.conclusion: Out of scope - root cause is in external dependency

severityAudit.recommendation: Downgrade to Low/QA or mark as Out of Scope. If kept, reframe as informational recommendation to add return value verification.
severityAudit.notes: The approvePhlimbo() function exists for owner to set approval. This is an integration consideration, not a vulnerability in the audited code.

severityAudit.title: All-or-Nothing Claim Design Creates Griefing Vector

analysis.assetRisk: No direct fund loss - yield accumulates but temporarily inaccessible
analysis.attackPath: Valid - Single paused token blocks all claims. This is a design flaw, not attack.
analysis.conditions: Owner pauses any token for legitimate reason (e.g., depeg event). All strategies become unclaimable.
analysis.impact: Protocol availability impacted - claim() function blocked for all users until all tokens unpaused

severityAudit.agreementReason: Correctly fits Medium criteria: protocol function (claim) is impacted, availability is affected, no direct asset theft, real scenario (token pausing for depegs is expected use case).
severityAudit.impactAssessment: medium - denial of service on claim function
severityAudit.recommendation: Keep as Medium. Recommend: skip paused tokens instead of reverting, or provide selective claim function per strategy.
severityAudit.notes: This is NOT admin mistake - owner may have legitimate reason to pause one token. The flaw is that pausing ONE token blocks ALL claims.

overstatements.reason: Requires admin misconfiguration - hypothetical attack path
Root cause is external contract (Phlimbo) - out of scope
